title: CMMS work-order client: retries, Retry-After and idempotency keys
scenario: The edge kit raises a draft work order in Corvane's CMMS when an anomaly is confirmed. The prototype's single POST lost orders during the CMMS's nightly 503s and duplicated them when a response was lost. One anomaly must mean one work order, always.
task: Idempotency key derived from machine and alert window
One retry loop: timeouts, retryable errors only, full-jitter backoff, Retry-After, budget
OAuth client credentials with caching, expiry refresh and one refresh on 401
Pydantic WorkOrder results and complete pagination
acceptance: 40 anomalies through 30% faults create exactly 40 work orders
Retry-After in seconds and HTTP-date honoured; no retry on 422; budget enforced
Timeout on every call; token refresh paths; pagination complete
ANSWER.md explains why the key, not the retries, prevents duplicates
